scope: internal development acceptance; disposable loopback browser, Spring HTTP and MySQL
browser_actions: Employee creates and submits a quantity request; administrator approves its fixed version
Warehouse operator claims the whole request and allocates assets 10 and 11
Operator physically delivers asset 10 to the test office and records inspection evidence
Asset ledger shows both formal storage and temporary physical destination
Operator registers recovery; backend is killed and restarted with the same database
Authenticated session, assignment, locks and recovery history survive reload
Final candidate backend is restarted; detail times now include UTC Z
Recovery remains disabled with code and inspection filled until actual-return checkbox is checked
Operator confirms physical recovery and inspection of asset 10, then cancels unhanded allocation 11
Cancelled request remains readable by its former assigned operator; ledger shows storage and no current temporary destination
cleanup: Owned backend, web server, MySQL container and its inspected anonymous volume removed
limits: Browser stack contains only synthetic accounts and disposable assets
Receiver page handlers separately reach actual HTTP/MySQL through an explicit loopback WeChat test adapter
No real SMS provider, external WeChat, external HTTPS or real device acceptance
No remote CI, formal QA or shared/production migration evidence
